steps.text: Bring water to a boil in a saucepan. Stir in rice. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer until liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes. Set aside.
Heat peanut oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add onions, bell pepper, garlic, and red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 3 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high. Stir in cooked rice, green onions, and soy sauce; cook and stir for 1 minute.
Add peas and cook for 1 minute more.
Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil and garnish with peanuts.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetable Fried Rice
raw_recipe.description: This vegetable fried rice is a quick dish that combines nutty brown rice with bell peppers, peas, and onions seasoned with sesame oil and soy sauce.
raw_recipe.name: Vegetable Fried Rice

review.reviewBody: Loved this. Omitted the peanut oil and used the sesame oil for stir-frying. Omitted the peanuts. Used edamame instead of canned peas and added matchstick carrots and a little egg substitute. We will definitely make this again. By the way, it made 5 side dish servings. Thanks, Verona.
I didn't put chilli flakes and peanut. I used chilli oil for frying the vegetables and I added one shredded carrot and fresh been sprouts. I also seasoned with ginger powder. It tastes amazing.

this was great! i used brown basmati rice, and added mushrooms and a frozen peas, carrots and string beans medley. i also only used one teaspoon of peanut oil. i like my rice a little hard so i left it in my cast iron pan for a little while. it was delicious and easy.

I added two scrambled eggs to the vegetable mix prior to adding in the rice to keep it like a traditional fried rice. I also replaced the bell pepper with an orange (sweet) pepper due to flavor preference.

Sauté onion, frozen peas, frozen corn and green,red and yellow pepper in sesame oil, added 2 scrambled eggs before I added the rice, then the cooked long grain brown rice and soy sauce. Served with Schwans lime chicken breasts! Hubby loved it, he said I could make it anytime!
I substituted veggie broth for water. The flavour from the broth really enhances the recipe. Also do add the peanuts they give it a crunch but wait until the last minute to do so.

It really needed some carrots so when I was all done I chopped up some carrots and stir fried them seperately and added them to the recipe! I also used frozen peas instead of canned (more nutricious) and added them with the onions and pepper! Next time I might put half of the pepper flakes just because my kids thought it was spicy but it wasn't too spicy for me and I'm not big on a lot of spice! I also added some chicken for some protein and we had this as a meal instead of a side!!! It was so very yummy! Even without my adjustments it was really good I just thought carrots would add nutrition and some bulk since it was the only course!!!

****Now that ive made this ohhhh I don't know....100+ times I wanted to add a few things! This recipe is so easy to adjust to your liking! First of all if you aren't vegan you can take 1-2 eggs, beat them and add them in last then stir fry until eggs are cooked! Be sure to get the veggies in there right away once chicken is in there or you will end up with crunchy veggies... unless of course you like crunchy veggies! I put chopped chicken in and imeadiately start chopping and adding veggies! We also use brown rice! I cook 2 cups dry rice seperately in my rice cooked then just blend it all together before adding sesame oil or seeds!

This was a hit! My husband loves Chinese food so I wanted to try making it instead of doing take out. We had store bought sesame chicken and I made the fried rice. I had all ingredients except sesame oil, so I substituted with peanut oil. Turned out great! I would suggest to add the soy sauce in increments - pour a bit then stir and repeat. I ended up not using all of it because it would have soaked the rice and overpowered the great flavors.

This was so amazing! I adjusted the recipe slightly to our families tastes; like carrot instead of bell pepper, more garlic, and red pepper flakes. Nothing that upset the balance much. It was a lot of prep so give yourself the time, took me about an hour of getting everything measured out and ready to go. But the cooking was quick, maybe 10 minutes or so. Next time I make this I will make a double batch and freeze some for a later date. It reheats great in the microwave.

Delicious! I followed the recipe exactly except for two things- slightly less onion (family preference) and I added two fried eggs, chopped into small pieces. It was a huge hit. I used it as a side to a miso cod dish.

This is a great start! I used grape seed oil instead of peanut, added minced ginger, daikon radish, and cabbage and bok choy near the end. I scrambled 2 eggs with a pinch of sugar and salt and poured them in after the peppers. Also, I used cashews instead of peanuts, and sprinkled on sesame seeds. It was just my perfect idea of what fried rice should be, and my husband agrees!
Very good! I used mixed vegetables and two scrambled eggs. Not sure why that was left out of the original recipe. I also threw in a teaspoon of curry which added to the color and flavor.
I added Spam and a package of mixed vegetables to it and it was great.

This was simple to fix and fairly quick too. I already had regular long grain rice in the cooker steaming. I didn't have peanuts. I'm not sure I liked the flavor of bell peppers in this. Other than the bell pepper, everything else was fine. The crushed red pepper was different from the usual, but it worked.

This was not my favorite fried rice recipe. I made as is and it was a little boring when I tasted so I added some diced carrots and egg. Also added some more sesame oil. It helped, but, something was missing. I will not make this one again.

A good recipe but I didn't make it exactly according to the recipe. I used toasted sesame oil, sweet potatoes instead of peas and a pinch of dried ground ginger. It is a really good recipe that can be modified many different ways.
This was a pretty tasty recipe. I did add egg and toasted almonds. The non-begs added chicken. I would definitely make this again!

I enjoyed making this recipe. The first time I did use the brown rice but for the second time I used white rice. I did substitute the peanut oil for walnut oil and didn't use peanuts either and I also used frozen mixed vegetables instead of just peas and a yellow pepper. But over all it was a very good recipe. Thanks for sharing.

I loved this recipe! I made it for the first time last night. I didn't have peanut oil so I used olive oil and I left out the green peppers. Also, I cooked the rice in a rice cooker and not on the stove. I came out great! I love the flavor, I think it's better than takeout.
